title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN placed as the enemy hero: Salah ad-Din lived 1137-1193 in Egypt/Syria and never set foot in Iberia; the in-game text even calls the foe 'Saladin's Emir', compounding the error. AoE2 offers alternatives (e.g. a generic Sultan/King unit, a renamed Castle-unit hero) so this was entirely avoidable.

28 CAMEL_RIDER for the Muslim side: Andalusi taifa and even Almoravid forces in Iberia fought as light javelin cavalry (jinetes), Berber infantry and heavy horse; massed camelry is North African/Levantine, not peninsular. Light Cavalry/Knights/Skirmishers were available in the engine.
31 CAVALRY_ARCHER as the enemy core: horse-archery was not a characteristic Andalusi/Almoravid arm; this is a steppe/Turkic template.

KING units in both Player Two and Player Three rosters represent nobody in the historical situation (al-Mutamin is voiced in text but never placed as a distinct figure), and give a European monarch model to Muslim taifa rulers.

A single monolithic 'Almoravid emir' enemy for the whole 1081-1094 span: the Almoravids only crossed to Iberia in 1086 and El Cid's Zaragoza-era opponents were Christian (Aragon, Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona) as often as Muslim; none of those belligerents appear at all.

issues_found: SALADIN is placed as the antagonist and is the primary victory target. Saladin (1137-1193, Egypt/Syria) has nothing to do with 11th-century Iberia; the historical opponents were the taifa of Lerida/Al-Mundir, Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona, and later the Almoravid emir Yusuf ibn Tashufin. The engine ships no Almoravid hero, but a renamed generic King/Cavalry unit was available and would have been correct; importing a different named hero from the wrong century and region is avoidable error.
In-game text names 'Saladin's Emir' and 'the emir of the Almoravids' interchangeably, conflating two unrelated dynasties.

Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture and unit rosters are not anchored to Iberian/Moorish appearance at all — an avoidable omission given Spanish and Saracen/Berber-flavoured civs exist.

Enemy composition is 28 Camel Riders plus 31 Cavalry Archers; Andalusi and Almoravid armies in Iberia fought as Berber light horse and jinetes, not camel cavalry, and mass cavalry archers are equally out of place for the peninsula.

None of the campaign's actual turning points appear: the victory at Almenar (1082) for Al-Mutamin, the defeat of Sancho Ramirez, the Battle of Tevar/Morella (1084) against Berenguer Ramon II, or the two-year siege and capture of Valencia in 1094.
The plot substitutes invented generic beats — 'raider outpost', 'bandits', 'Ambusher', 'Traitor King', an unnamed fortress — for documented campaigns.
Valencia, the stated goal of the brief, exists nowhere as a placed settlement; there is no city to conquer, only a Castle/Keep/stone-wall compound belonging to Saladin.
Victory is DESTROY_OBJECT on Saladin (or destroying a gate), i.e. decapitating an anachronistic enemy leader, rather than taking possession of Valencia — El Cid's actual and defining achievement.
Defeat on the death of Player 3's KING (standing in for Al-Mutamin) misrepresents history: Al-Mutamin died of natural causes in 1085 and El Cid's career continued regardless.
GAIA decoration includes ROMAN_RUINS and a SKELETON as the 'old ruins' clue site — generic dungeon-crawl set dressing rather than anything Iberian.

SALADIN is placed as the enemy hero and the primary victory target; Saladin (d. 1193, Ayyubid Egypt/Syria) never fought in Iberia and belongs to a different culture and a century later than the Almoravid emirs (Yusuf ibn Tashfin) or the taifa rivals El Cid actually faced. The engine offers other Muslim/Iberian-appropriate heroes or a simple renamed generic unit, so this was avoidable.
Both active players are set to civilization RANDOM, so architecture and unit sets are not fixed as Spanish and Saracen/Berber; the Iberian setting is left to chance.
Al-Mutamin of Zaragoza, El Cid's actual patron, exists only as a dialogue line and an anonymous KING; Alfonso VI and Yusuf ibn Tashfin are absent entirely.

Player 2's army is 28 camel riders and 31 cavalry archers with no infantry — a steppe/Saracen composition rather than Almoravid Berber infantry-and-lancer forces, and vastly outnumbering any force El Cid faced at this stage.

Central plot beats are invented: a 'Traitor King' betrayal, a generic raider outpost, and a rescued ally, none of which correspond to the Zaragoza campaigns (Almenar, Morella) or the 1094 siege of Valencia.
Valencia — the stated culmination of the brief — is nowhere in the victory conditions; the campaign instead ends at a generic 'enemy fortress' with an Almoravid/Saladin emir.
Alternative victory fires on destroying a GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH inside an arbitrary map area, an objective the history does not single out.
Defeat is tied to the death of a nameless Player 3 KING labelled 'key ally'; El Cid's fortunes never hinged on protecting a Muslim king's life in this way.
